qt: to the Commission Joachim Streit (Renew) Subject:

Belgium intends to introduce a vignette for cars by 1 May 2027, which will also apply on numerous national and regional roads. At the same time, a reform of vehicle taxation is envisaged, which could lighten the tax burden for Belgian car owners. This raises questions of compatibility with EU law. On 18 June 2019, the European Court of Justice declared the German car toll to be contrary to EU law, as the simultaneous relief of domestic vehicle owners via the vehicle tax led to indirect discrimination against foreign drivers. The Belgian project could also lead to an additional financial burden, in particular for citizens of border regions, while Belgian car owners may be economically compensated by the tax reform. What possibilities does the Commission see for preventing a disproportionate burden on citizens in cross-border regional traffic (or, more specifically, between Belgium and Germany) and, if necessary, for promoting exemptions for local border traffic?
